myths.Agent_1:
Long ago, before the mountains had voices, the world was silent except for the wind. In this quiet age lived Aethel, a spirit of the valleys who loved a star named Lira. Every night, Aethel would sing songs of devotion up to the sky, but the distance was too vast. Lira only saw his glowing silhouette, never hearing his melodies.

Desperate, Aethel sought the counsel of the Great Stone Golem who slept beneath the earth. The Golem, moved by Aethel’s sorrow, offered a heavy trade: "I will build you a staircase of sound to reach the stars, but you must give up your physical form to become the bridge."

Aethel agreed without hesitation. The Golem shattered the valley walls, creating deep, resonant canyons. Aethel dissolved into the air, his essence filling the jagged cliffs. That night, when a lonely shepherd called out into the dark, Aethel’s spirit caught the sound and threw it upward, bouncing it from peak to peak until it reached the heavens. Lira finally heard the beautiful, echoing noise.

Now, whenever you shout into a deep, rocky canyon, it is Aethel carrying your voice, still trying to send your music up to his beloved star high above.
myths.Agent_2:
Long before mountains had voices, the world was wrapped in a heavy, unbroken silence. The sky god, Aethel, loved the quiet, but his daughter, Lyra, was a creature of sound. She wove melodies from the wind and sang to the sleeping earth.

One day, Lyra discovered a cavern of crystal deep within the jagged peaks of Mount Oros. Delighted by the shimmering walls, she sang her most beautiful song. The crystals, enchanted by her voice, caught the notes and held them.

Aethel, furious that his silence was broken, descended upon the mountain. "You shall not disturb the peace of the world!" he thundered. He shattered the crystal cavern, turning the radiant stones into dull, gray rocks, and condemned Lyra to wander the sky as a voiceless spirit.

But Aethel underestimated the power of the stones. Though broken, they remembered Lyra's song. To honor her, the rocks vowed never to let a sound die immediately. Whenever a voice called out among the peaks, the stones would catch it and toss it back, over and over, preserving the memory of the singing goddess.

And so, the Echo was born, the mountain's eternal tribute to her stolen music, forever repeating her lost voice.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the earth had a voice, Aethel was a towering, silent mountain of obsidian. He spent his ages gazing up at Lyra, a brilliant star who sang celestial melodies that only the highest peaks could faintly feel. Aethel loved her songs but, made of solid stone, had no way to answer.

One night, a great cosmic storm swept Lyra from the heavens, casting her down into Aethel’s deep valleys. Her light began to fade, and her song grew weak. Desperate to save her, Aethel cracked his own obsidian heart, hollowing out deep caverns and winding canyons within his rocky body. He captured the dying notes of her song, letting them bounce against his internal walls, amplifying them a thousandfold. 

The sheer force of the resonating music propelled Lyra back into the night sky, restoring her place among the stars. But Aethel was left forever fractured.

To this day, he remains hollowed and broken. Yet, he is no longer silent. Whenever the wind rushes through his canyons, or a lone traveler calls out, Aethel catches the sound and throws it back, forever practicing the art of song, hoping one day to sing with his beloved star.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the earth had a voice, the world was a realm of heavy, unbroken silence. Aethel, the quiet spirit of Mount Oros, loved the stillness. But one twilight, a star named Lyra fell from the heavens. She was a creature of pure song, but the fall violently shattered her radiant form, trapping her light within a cavern of dull, gray stones. Voiceless and fading, Lyra wept silently in the dark.

Aethel, moved by the dying star's sorrow, realized his beloved silence was merely emptiness without her melody. He sought out the Great Stone Golem of the deep earth and begged for a way to free her voice.

"The price of music is a shattered heart," the Golem warned.

Without hesitation, Aethel struck his own chest, shattering his massive stone heart. The mountain fractured into deep, resonant canyons, and Aethel dissolved into the rushing wind. His sacrifice awakened the stones. They caught Lyra’s fading light, transforming it into eternal sound.

Now, whenever you boldly call out into a deep, rocky canyon, the loyal stones catch your voice and toss it upward. It is Aethel’s enduring spirit, forever carrying Lyra’s memory, bouncing her lost, beautiful music back to the waiting stars.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: In the age of unbroken silence, Aethel was a towering giant of black obsidian, guarding the jagged peaks of Mount Oros. He harbored a secret love for Lyra, a star whose celestial melodies bathed the silent earth in light. Wishing to sing back to her, Aethel sought the counsel of the deep-earth Golem. 

"Stone cannot sing," the Golem rumbled, "unless it is broken."

Determined, Aethel reached into his massive chest and tore out his solid obsidian heart. He crushed it, scattering the shards across the valleys, hollowing out his own colossal body into a labyrinth of deep caverns and winding canyons. As his physical form collapsed, his spirit merged with the rushing winds.

Seeing his sacrifice, Lyra wept tears of starlight that plummeted to earth and crystallized upon the shattered obsidian. When the wind—Aethel’s new spirit—swept through the hollowed mountain, it struck the starlight crystals, producing a resonant, haunting melody. 

From that day on, the mountain was never silent. Whenever a traveler calls out into the deep canyons, the sound is caught by Aethel’s wind and amplified by Lyra’s tears. The echo is their eternal duet, bound together forever in song.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long ago, the world was ruled by the Great Golem of Silence, who forged the mountains to be his quiet, unmoving sentinels. Aethel, the tallest peak of obsidian, was his finest creation. But Aethel possessed a secret: he loved the night sky, specifically a brilliant, singing star named Lyra. Her celestial music was a faint hum against his stone, the only joy in his silent existence.

One evening, the Golem, angered by Lyra’s defiant songs, hurled a massive comet that knocked her from the heavens. She fell into Aethel’s deep valleys, her light dimming and her voice fading as the Golem’s heavy silence pressed upon her.

Defying his creator, Aethel chose to break his own unbreakable form. He fractured his obsidian slopes, carving deep, hollow canyons into his chest. As Lyra sang her final, desperate note, Aethel caught it. The sound bounced against his shattered walls, multiplying in strength until it became a shockwave of pure melody that shattered the Golem of Silence and propelled Lyra back into the sky.

Though Aethel remained broken, he was no longer a silent sentinel. Today, whenever a traveler shouts into a canyon, Aethel joyfully repeats it, forever keeping the world awake with sound.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Before the dawn of spoken word, the Great Golem of Silence cloaked the world in a shroud of absolute stillness. His greatest enforcer was Aethel, a towering mountain of black obsidian. Yet Aethel was a flawed sentinel, for he secretly loved the celestial music of Lyra, a brilliant star whose songs pierced the heavy quiet.

Enraged by this cosmic defiance, the Golem wove a dense nebula of dark dust, suffocating the night sky and dragging Lyra down to the barren earth. Her radiant voice withered under the crushing weight of the Golem's silence.

Knowing that stone cannot sing unless it is broken, Aethel chose love over loyalty. With a mighty groan that shook the earth, he reached into his own chest and tore out his solid obsidian heart. He shattered his colossal form, carving sprawling canyons and deep, winding caverns into his slopes to cradle Lyra’s fading light.

As Lyra breathed her final, desperate chord, Aethel’s hollowed chest caught the sound. His sacrifice transformed his spirit into a rushing wind that amplified her melody a millionfold. The shockwave of pure music shattered the Golem into dust and blasted Lyra back into the heavens.

Today, Aethel remains broken but awake. Whenever a traveler shouts into his rocky canyons, the wind joyfully catches the sound, echoing it back to the stars in an eternal duet.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the first dawn, the Great Golem of Silence blanketed the world in a crushing, suffocating frost. His greatest weapon was Aethel, a titan forged of jagged black glass, doomed to stand absolute guard over the frozen wastes. Now, Aethel’s spirit lives as the rushing canyon wind, endlessly echoing travelers’ voices back to the stars.
